locations.name: Grand Preceptory of Saint Eccles
locations.blurb: The principal house of the Church of Saint Eccles and its foremost training center, a sandstone complex over six hundred feet long that can be seen for miles.

locations.name: Seawall
locations.blurb: A wall of immense fitted stone blocks across the narrowest part of the peninsula west of the village, said to have been laid out by Sir Valory Eccles himself.

locations.name: Royal Muster Hall
locations.blurb: A stone hall with a gatehouse, stables, and yard at the junction of the coastal royal road and the road north into the village. Mounted patrols begin and end their rounds here.

locations.name: Sea Cider Inn
locations.blurb: A welcoming inn just east of the crossroads with a courtyard and its own house-made sea cider, run by the gullfolk Brinefeather family for generations.

locations.name: Johunn & Johunn Milling
locations.blurb: A windmill, warehouses, and fruit press on the lane from the crossroads to Nereth Bay, owned by the goliath brothers Harek and Borun Johunn.

locations.name: Training Grounds
locations.blurb: Expansive fields east of the Grand Preceptory where squires, clerics, wardens, and paladins train from dawn to dusk. Visitors may watch from designated areas.

locations.name: Queensland Orchards
locations.blurb: Nearly three-quarters of a mile of orchards east of the village, owned by the Queensland Farmers' Union and worked by leasing families, famous for apples, pears, cherries, and cider.

locations.name: Bastelin Manor
locations.blurb: The manor of House Bastelin on the southern road, residence of the Royal Reeve, Lord Bavar Bastelin, a stoneheart mustelin.

locations.name: Shore Road North
locations.blurb: A paved royal road that leaves the village to the east and curves northeast around Nereth Bay for twenty miles before decaying into the Dry Fells.

locations.name: Ohlmith Trail
locations.blurb: The royal highway south through the orchards and farmland, then nearly two hundred miles east to Ohlmith and the Queen's Road, passing the market town of Crannick.

locations.name: Shore Road South
locations.blurb: A paved royal highway along the western coast for nearly a hundred miles to the port city of Annapore, passing the gates of the Grand Preceptory.

locations.name: Main Gates
locations.blurb: The busiest gate, on the southern side, where Crown infantry inspect travelers and levy tolls. Gatewatch Keep stands just beyond the walls.

locations.name: West Gate
locations.blurb: The busiest of the local gates, opening toward the fisheries and docks. Local volunteers, not Crown soldiers, keep it, and the mood is relaxed.

locations.name: East Gate
locations.blurb: The quietest gate, opening onto the sheltered shore of Nereth Bay and used mostly by local farmers, orchard workers, and villagers headed for the beaches.

locations.name: North Gate
locations.blurb: A volunteer-watched gate serving the northern workshops, the lighthouse, private piers, and Beacon Spit. Rarely crowded, but one of the most used.

locations.name: The Pink Pearl Inn
locations.blurb: A three-story wattle-and-daub inn near the heart of the village, run by the gullfolk innkeeper Gohlo Konono, where fishers, farmers, and off-duty soldiers gather.

locations.name: North Point Sundry
locations.blurb: A general store, outfitter, and chandlery run by the riverheart mustelin Arno Graybrook, who seems able to produce any item on request.

locations.name: Queensland Exchange
locations.blurb: A timber-framed market hall with a permanent indoor market and the offices of the Queensland Farmers' Union and many guilds. The Adventurers' Guild keeps a small agency here.

locations.name: Alghorand House
locations.blurb: The stone residence and administrative offices of the Royal Reeve, overlooking the village square, with a Royal Adventuring Society briefing officer stationed from time to time.

locations.name: Crown Barracks
locations.blurb: A substantial multi-story stone barracks in the northern part of the Royal Compound, home to the Algarian Crown Infantry stationed at Pistil Point.

locations.name: Shrine of the Humble Virtues
locations.blurb: The largest building inside the walls, a red granite shrine to the Resonant Virtues with chapels for many faiths, served by visiting clergy on rotation.

locations.name: Public Docks
locations.blurb: The village's main waterfront for visiting ships, just south of the fisheries. With no deepwater harbor, a launch and longboat ferry people and cargo from ships at anchor.

locations.name: Myonis Beach
locations.blurb: A sheltered beach on the lee side of the peninsula, good for swimming, picnics, and watching Lustre rise, with a modest public pier.

locations.name: Pistil Point Fisheries
locations.blurb: Two privately owned fisheries side by side, overseen by the Fishermen's Compact. One packs fresh fish for quick transport, and the other brines, smokes, and cures.

locations.name: Hrumm Ironworks
locations.blurb: The largest smithy on the peninsula, just outside the North Gate, owned by the goliath blacksmith Moder Hrumm and supplier to the Grand Preceptory.

locations.name: Point Lighthouse
locations.blurb: An eighty-foot dressed-stone lighthouse at the rocky northern tip, second tallest structure on the peninsula, kept by the gullfolk Toolah Tattoppo.

locations.name: Beacon Spit
locations.blurb: A chain of gravel and sand islets stretching five hundred feet into the sea past the lighthouse, linked by two rope bridges, and the site of a yearly bonfire when Lustre rises.
